decisions.statement: Every composed body reaches the checkout through the tracking landing.
Every body one call composes lands in one commit or lands in no commit.
No body reaches the landing through a scratch file.
A key on its way into akasha is written in camel here rather than by a caller.
A day that has not been written is not a day that is empty.
A patch is composed from the page there merged with the values the caller gave.
No row beside a day page is landed here.
Another writer moving the day page between the read and the write is expected.
A landing refused for that reason is composed again over the body as it now is.
A landing is tried four times before it is answered as refused.
A landing refused for any other reason is answered without being tried again.
Another writer landing the very body this one composed is expected too.
A landing refused because the page already holds that body is answered as landed.
The day then says what the caller meant it to say, which is what the caller asked for.

definition: how a day page is landed into the akasha page store
